items.basis: Companies Act 2013 Schedule II Part C: general plant & machinery other than continuous process plant = 15 years; continuous process plant = 25 years (G.S.R. 237(E), 31.03.2014).

Schedule II note: useful life is based on single shift; for the period an asset works double shift depreciation increases by 50%, triple shift by 100%, pro rata to days worked; not for assets marked NESD. Useful life itself does not change.
15-year SLM = 6.67%/yr; +100% for triple shift = 13.33%/yr => equivalent 7.5-year straight-line life at 3 shifts all year.
items.notes: Recommended statutory basis for a 3-shift MHR. An 8-10 yr 'economic life' costing convention: no authoritative Indian source found; the ICAI-style worked example uses 10 years (exam material).

Tool limits: WebFetch and direct downloads were blocked (DNS/egress policy) so every figure comes from search-result extracts of the cited pages; PDFs (Knight Frank, CREDAI, NSE filings) were not opened directly. Re-verify before locking.

Capex evidence is thin: only Jyoti CNC's reported realisation, SLTL's starting price and one Indian HPDC maker's list are producer-grade. Press, IMM, sand line, furnace, forging, gear, grinder and all IMPORTED machine prices were not found from an acceptable source; marketplace listings are given as cross-checks only, per RULES.

Strong conclusion regardless of the gaps: the current India book carries UK capital (implied capex in crores for a VMC/lathe, e.g. VMC3 depreciation Rs 36.8 lakh/yr; CNC lathe Rs 26.8 lakh/yr; drill Rs 18.7 lakh/yr; HAAS VF-2 Rs 25.4 lakh/yr) and UK hours (3,200 productive h vs ~5,000 at 3 shifts). Domestic Indian CNC machines sell at ~Rs 15-40 lakh. Every benchmark charge-out rate found (WITH operator and margin) for VMCs is Rs 250-1,500/h and CNC turning Rs 160-500/h, below the current machine-only figures (VMC3 Rs 3,419, HAAS VF-2 Rs 2,854, lathe Rs 2,490, drill Rs 1,840).
Inconsistency inside the current book: imm-200t (Rs 1,362/h) vs imm-200t-in (Rs 703/h) for the same class.
Imported machines: duty 8.25% non-creditable (BCD 7.5% + SWS) on CIF; IGST 18% creditable - so an imported machine's landed capex is ~CIF x 1.0825 + freight/installation (% not found).
